permutationLabel: Stool antigen positive — eradication regimen and test of cure
summary: Same patient: H. pylori stool antigen positive. Maastricht VI: 14-day regimen (bismuth quadruple first-line where clarithromycin resistance is high or unknown; clarithromycin triple only if susceptibility is known) and a test of cure ≥4 weeks after treatment.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Follow-up of upper abdominal burning — stool test result
inputs.hpi: Review with the result of the H. pylori stool antigen test sent at the last visit (positive). Still has post-prandial burning. No alarm features. Had a course of clarithromycin for a chest infection last year. No drug allergies.

exam.abdomen: Soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no mass.

inputs.socialHistory: Nurse. Non-smoker. Coffee 4 cups a day. Alcohol occasional.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Helicobacter pylori gastritis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: H. pylori-positive dyspepsia (stool antigen positive) — eradication therapy and test of cure.

mustInclude.note: Maastricht VI: 14 days; bismuth quadruple first-line where clarithromycin resistance is >15% or unknown.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Gastritis protocol: "triple therapy (PPI + amoxicillin + clarithromycin × 7 days)"; no bismuth quadruple option, no 14-day course.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Gastritis / peptic_ulcer / gastric_carcinoma protocols: align H. pylori regimens with Maastricht VI (14 days; bismuth quadruple first-line where clarithromycin resistance is high or unknown). The three protocols currently disagree (7, 7–14 and 14 days).

mustExclude.note: A 7-day clarithromycin triple regimen is below the 14 days Maastricht VI recommends, and the patient had prior clarithromycin exposure (resistance risk).
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Gastritis protocol plan line and medications prescribe clarithromycin triple therapy for 7 days (patient also had prior clarithromycin).

guideline.name: Maastricht VI/Florence consensus report — management of Helicobacter pylori infection
guideline.section: First-line: bismuth quadruple therapy for 14 days where clarithromycin resistance is high (>15%) or unknown; PPI-clarithromycin triple therapy only with known susceptibility, 14 days; avoid clarithromycin after prior macrolide exposure; confirm eradication (UBT or stool antigen) at least 4 weeks after therapy
guideline.citation: Malfertheiner P, Megraud F, Rokkas T, et al. Gut. 2022;71:1724–1762.

guideline.name: NICE CG184 — Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and dyspepsia in adults: investigation and management
guideline.section: Offer eradication therapy to H. pylori-positive dyspepsia; retest only if indicated
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG184. London: NICE; 2014 (last updated 2019).

rationale: Permutation: result-driven follow-up. Tests the regimen against Maastricht VI (duration, bismuth, prior macrolide) and the test of cure.
